title: "Part 4 – Replication and preregistration"

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/housing-one-day-open-science.html#/part-4-replication-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 leaves the original file behind. After a short look at how far the answer moves when the analysis changes on those same data, it turns to the replication that SCORE ran with new emails and new names, reads the plan that was registered before the first email went out, and ends on a preregistration of your own, filled in before any result exists and not run. The part takes ninety minutes.

## 1. The curve of the claim

**On the slides.** The curve holds the 64 specifications that the course judged justifiable on these data, ranked from the largest gap to the smallest. The published result of the original authors (OAs) and the five analysts are placed on it.

To go further: [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd).

## 2. The replication

**On the slides.** The SCORE replication was a preregistered audit of 3,050 housing authorities with new names. The slides show what it found, compare the original study and the replication row by row, and set out the power of the two designs. They end on the three Rs on this paper and on what separates robustness from replicability.

To go further: [the replication](../../cases/housing/index.qmd#sec-replication) in the case study.

## 3. The preregistration of the replication

**On the slides.** The slides show what the preregistration of the replication fixed, what the final report added, and how a reader can tell the two apart. They then ask what a preregistration fixes in general, and what it leaves open.

## 4. Archives and registrations

**On the slides.** The slides show where a reanalysis is archived and registered, the preregistration of Multi100 itself, and the two preregistration templates. You then search the public record of the case for the replication report, for three minutes, and the slides map the eight AsPredicted questions onto the decisions of the analysis.

To go further: [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd).

## 5. Task 5 – The preregistration

[Open the browser lab at Task 5](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-5-preregistration){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Fill in the preregistration cell, without running the analysis. It asks for the claim, the data and what you already know about them, one option for each decision on the `my_` lines, a sentence from your estimand statement on why your choices answer the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Copy the block into your notes. Nothing is fitted and nothing is sent, and if you run the cell, it only checks your choices and prints the block. Then swap with a neighbour and ask whether they could run your analysis from your block alone.

## 6. The close

**On the slides.** The day closes on what you take with you, and the feedback form.

**By the end of the part** you can say what a replication with new data adds to a reproduction and to a check of robustness, you can read a replication report against its preregistration, and you have a preregistration block of your own, filled in before any result existed.
